what: Task 3 CG/AMG iterative-EQS spike: PRE-REGISTERED protocol. Written and committed BEFORE any iterative solver code exists.

step_0_direct_path_own_floor_MEASURED_FI.why: The plan requires reporting the direct path's own rtol floor BEFORE choosing an acceptance tolerance, so the iterative gate is measured against the incumbent rather than against a number picked to be passable.
step_0_direct_path_own_floor_MEASURED_FI.method: solve3d/adjoint.py SteadyEqs.solve_state: PETSc preonly+LU followed by N_REFINE iterative-refinement sweeps; res_norm = ||b - A x|| / ||b|| after refinement. Cube, pre-L0 geometry pinned (precomp s_*=0), 3 repeats, best and median wall reported.
step_0_direct_path_own_floor_MEASURED_FI.headline: the direct path solves to a relative residual of ~1e-19, NOT ~1e-10
step_0_direct_path_own_floor_MEASURED_FI.consequence_stated_before_measuring_the_: forward.py's existing KSP_ITER preset uses ksp_rtol 1e-10, which is NINE TO TEN ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE looser than the incumbent floor. adjoint.py records that the refinement sweeps 'buy roughly two decades of FD headroom', so a 1e-10 iterative solve is expected a priori to damage the Phase B FD gate. The spike must therefore test the FD gate at the iterative tolerance, not just field agreement, and 1e-10 is NOT assumed acceptable.

primary.note: CG is valid only if the operator is Hermitian positive definite; the EQS operator is COMPLEX SYMMETRIC (A^T = A), which is NOT the same thing. If CG fails or stalls this is the reason, and the fallback is GMRES+GAMG, which is what forward.py's existing KSP_ITER preset already uses.
primary.precedent: D1 spike reported 229-431x; that speedup is the hypothesis under test here, not an assumption

solver_config.rtol_selection_rule: the LOOSEST rtol in the sweep that passes BOTH acceptance gates below; if none passes, the recommendation is to keep the direct path and say so

gate_1_field_agreement.quantity: relative L2 difference of the EQS potential V and of Q_rf between iterative and direct solves on the same assembled operator
gate_1_field_agreement.tolerance_rule: MEASURED, not invented: the iterative-vs-direct difference must be no larger than the direct path's own level-to-level change across the coarse->mid refinement, which is the smallest difference the incumbent itself cannot resolve. That number is computed in the spike and recorded before any verdict.

gate_2_fd_regate.what: re-run ONE Phase B FD probe with the iterative path in the loop
gate_2_fd_regate.standard: the frozen protocol in solve3d/results/phase_b_protocol.json, unchanged; the gradient must still meet its recorded rel_err standard
gate_2_fd_regate.why_this_is_the_binding_gate: field agreement at 1e-10 can look fine while the FD headroom is destroyed, because FD differences J(s+eps)-J(s-eps) are exactly where a loose solve tolerance shows up. A gradient that no longer passes is a FAIL regardless of how good the fields look.

acceptance.adjoint_gets_the_same_treatment: the A^H system (Phase B reuses the forward factorization; an iterative path must be shown to preserve that, or the adjoint solve cost must be reported separately and honestly)

benchmark_protocol.scheduling: compute-scheduling convention: announce, 1-min load < 20, one heavy slot
benchmark_protocol.statistic: best and median wall, both reported
benchmark_protocol.speedup_definition: direct wall / iterative wall on the SAME assembled operator and the same machine state

flag_and_default.implementation: behind a flag; default stays DIRECT and the off-path must be bit-identical to today
flag_and_default.default_flip: goes to Matt with the measured evidence; this lane does not flip it (EQS-02 precedent)

null_result_is_valid: if CG/AMG cannot reach a tolerance that preserves the FD gate, the honest outcome is that the direct path stays and the D1 speedup does not transfer to this operator. That is a finding, not a failure to be worked around.
